A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIR/VIR research. The complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite added sections and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Light Tunnel and VitalDB experiments, including prediction errors, robustness curves, and tracking correlations in Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds DRIG comparisons, assumption-violation tests, and an unlabeled-environment analysis.

M1.justification: The core MIR, VIR, and combined MIR–VIR objectives are retained. Appendix E newly sketches conditioning on observed covariates W and applying MIR/VIR within strata, while leaving full development to future work. Equations 12–13 also remove an extra 1/p penalty factor.

E1.justification: Coverage expands within the same datasets and populations. Section 7.3 adds RGB-to-sensor prediction on Light Tunnel and absolute stroke-volume prediction without subject-centering on VitalDB. These introduce different prediction requirements and causal conditions, but no new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: DRIG is newly evaluated in the centered VitalDB comparisons in Figures 4–5, alongside the retained Pooled-Ridge, GroupDRO, and oracle comparisons. AnchorReg also participates in the new uncentered VitalDB experiment. The original Light Tunnel comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing evaluation protocols are retained. New experiments use five labeled training environments for reversed Light Tunnel prediction, omit VitalDB centering with separately tuned mean/covariance penalties, and fix 20 labeled subjects while varying unlabeled subjects. Appendix G states a 0–80 range, whereas Figure 7 displays 20–80, leaving the zero-unlabeled condition unclear.

E4.justification: Section 7.3 and Appendix F add targeted tests of reversed causal direction and environment effects on the outcome. Appendix G separately tests the benefit of additional unlabeled environments while holding labeled data fixed. These substantially expand scrutiny of the assumptions and the central unlabeled-data mechanism beyond v1's analyses.

E5.justification: The existing 20 random selections of labeled environments/subjects and Figure 3's standard-error reporting are retained. Added figures use error bars, bands, or boxplots, but introduce no stated change to run counts, uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds DRIG results in Figures 4–5 and new results in Figures 6–7. Figure 6 shows MIR matching Pooled-Ridge under reversed prediction and modest MIR–VIR advantages over Pooled-Ridge/AnchorReg without centering. Figure 7 shows error declining through 60 unlabeled subjects, then increasing slightly at 80, contrary to the accompanying monotonicity claim. Original Light Tunnel results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E introduces Setting E.1, an observed-covariate SCM, and a conditional-independence argument for extending the framework. Proposition 5.1 now states the balanced-sampling condition already used in v1's Appendix A.4, correcting a statement/proof mismatch. The existing robustness theorems and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and central conclusion retain the same claims: unlabeled-data MIR/VIR regularization, worst-case guarantees over specified environment classes, and benefits on two real-world datasets. Additional evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the interpretation of applicability. Remark 3.2 includes dependence through latent confounding without a direct outcome-to-predictor edge. Remark 4.3 and Section 7.3 argue that cross-validation can suppress inappropriate regularization and explain residual bias when environments affect outcomes. The conclusion also adds unresolved nonparametric extensions and finite-sample bounds.

D1.justification: Appendix I adds DRIG's tuning grid from 10^-2 through 10^4. Appendix F documents the new tests and the separate MIR–VIR parameter grids, each {10^2, 10^3, 10^4, 10^5}. Existing experimental details are largely retained in renamed Appendices H–I; no new code or data access provision appears.

R1.justification: Related work adds Eastwood et al. (2023) on anti-causal domain generalization. The conclusion newly positions regression domain generalization as comparatively underexplored and the experimental setups as potential benchmarks. Shen et al. (2026), underlying DRIG, was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: revised remarks, new Section 7.3 and Appendices E–G, an expanded conclusion, acknowledgements, and publication-header edits. Earlier experimental appendices move from E–F to H–I. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multipanel stress-test Figure 6, unlabeled-environment Figure 7, and an observed-covariate causal diagram. Figures 4–5 gain DRIG displays. Figure 4a also changes quantile labels from ascending 0–100% to descending 100–0%, correcting their relationship to the displayed tail errors.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical scrutiny through a relevant DRIG comparison, assumption-violation tests, and an experiment holding labeled data fixed. It also aligns Proposition 5.1 with its existing proof and corrects Figure 4's quantile labels. These benefits outweigh limited new reporting problems: Appendix G claims a 0–80 sweep and monotonic improvement, while Figure 7 shows 20–80 and a final slight increase. The additions support a modest overall quality gain.
